video.title: Most Will Fail to Earn Money From AI Made Apps (Unless You Use This Strategy)

summary: Side Hustle Nation host Nick Loper interviews Steve (App Masters, 17 years in app marketing, now acquiring and building vibe-coded apps). Steve's playbook: find keywords people search in the App Store (ASO), unbundle a feature from big apps, build a one-feature app named after the keyword, use a hard paywall with copied competitor pricing, and optionally run a lifetime-deal growth hack or Apple Search Ads. He claims apps earning from about $200/month to $35k MRR, and says roughly 40% of apps he launches make money. Key takeaway: distribution (ASO) matters more than features.

ideas.name: Keyword-led single-feature iOS app portfolio (ASO-first)
ideas.one_liner: Research App Store keywords, vibe-code a one-feature app named after the keyword, rank via ASO, monetise with a paywall.
ideas.business_model: In-app subscriptions (weekly/yearly) or one-time purchases via App Store
ideas.customer: App Store users searching for a specific utility or feature, mostly iOS
ideas.problem: People want a simple tool for one task (converting JPEG to PDF, paraphrasing text, green noise sounds) and search the App Store for it
ideas.offer: A narrow single-purpose app whose name is the exact target keyword, with a hard paywall and free trial

pricing.model: Subscription, mostly weekly for one-time-use utilities and yearly for frequent-use apps; copy competitor pricing

price_points.label: Yearly plan with 7-day trial on Paraphrase

pricing.notes: Look at the top in-app purchases in Sensor Tower and copy the leader's most popular plan.

acquisition_channels.details: ASO: target keywords with traffic score about 30 and few competitors with the keyword in the title; put keyword in app name and first screenshot; ratings prompt for reviews.

quote.text: All you really need is a hundred downloads a day to have a six-figure business in the app space.
quote.speaker: Steve

acquisition_channels.details: Apple Search Ads exact-match keywords and Max Conversions campaigns at $10-20/day as plan C; Google Ads for cheaper Android downloads.
Google search for 'app' keywords also drives some downloads.

ideas.delivery: Software delivered via App Store; first version built with Claude Code in two to three days; Apple handles payments and refunds.
unit_economics_claims: A different app at $35,000 MRR with 12% trial start and 60% trial-to-paid
About 40% of launched apps make money (10 launches for 4 winners)
ideas.startup_cost: Not stated beyond the Apple developer account; ad spend optional ($10-20/day). Personal developer account can be used initially.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: JPEG to PDF app took 2-3 days to ship; a new app made $1,600 in its first month

acquisition.how: ASO and in-store ads are inbound and software-driven; keyword research and metadata tuning can be agent-run with occasional approval.

onboarding.how: Self-serve in-app onboarding and paywall with no human involved.

delivery.how: Software product; Claude Code can build and maintain, with occasional human review of App Store submissions.

billing.how: Apple handles subscriptions, billing and refunds.

support.how: Low volume (1-2 refund emails a week); templated reply directing users to Apple.

uk_applicability.notes: App Store works the same in the UK. UK developers need an Apple developer account, VAT/tax handling and a privacy policy; individual accounts are possible but UK trader-status disclosure applies.

risks: Apple review inconsistency over hard paywalls
Apple scrutiny of unusual download and review spikes

tactics.name: Unbundle a big app's secondary keyword
steps: Pull top-grossing apps on Sensor Tower
Find keywords they don't target, or that appear in their ads
Check ASO Mobile for traffic score about 30
Check search results for few apps with keyword in title and weak ratings
Build a one-feature app named after the keyword

quote.text: you unbuddle the big app and then you go, all right, what does the competition look like?
quote.speaker: Steve

tactics.name: Copy competitor pricing and plan type
steps: Open the competitor in Sensor Tower
Check the most popular in-app purchase
Copy price and weekly or yearly format
Use weekly with 3-day trial for one-time-use apps, yearly with 7-day trial for daily-use apps

tactics.name: Paywall conversion tweaks
steps: Use hard paywall in onboarding
Use the word 'Continue' instead of 'Subscribe'
Add 'No payment now' under the call to action
Show all plans in the same yearly price format
Use the word 'free' for premium features

quote.text: 30% increase in conversions with the word continue versus subscribe
quote.speaker: Steve

tactics.name: Fast MVP launch
steps: Prompt Claude Code for a single-feature app
Ship in 2-3 days even without a paywall or nice screenshots
Add privacy policy and terms
Launch on iOS under a personal account
Add paywall once downloads show up

tactics.name: Ratings prompt and ASO push
steps: Add the built-in iOS ratings prompt (about 1% of downloads leave reviews)
Ask a little later, e.g. day two
Optimise keyword and title
Optionally run a lifetime-deal push

warnings.warning: Many launched apps fail because keywords don't stick; the hit rate is about 40%.

warnings.warning: Android users reach more people but pay less, so launch on iOS first.
Apple emailed developers over abnormal download and review spikes from the lifetime offer.

lessons.lesson: Distribution is the hard part, not building; pick ideas where discovery is already built in through search demand.

quote.text: It's distribution is just so hard that it should be the number one thing you think about
quote.speaker: Steve

lessons.lesson: Validate demand by confirming an existing competitor makes money and people search for the keyword.
One narrow problem per app; more niche raises willingness to pay.

quote.text: The more niche you could be, the higher likelihood that people are going to pay for your app.
quote.speaker: Steve

lessons.lesson: Copy proven pricing instead of inventing your own.
Treat it as a portfolio: expect around 60% of launches to fail and ship many.
Don't over-engineer legal structure or branding early; start with a personal account and change later.
Low support load because Apple handles payments and refunds makes apps highly passive (about 1-2 hours a week for one app).
Leave growth headroom in an app you want to sell; buyers pay for potential.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with many specific figures, but shown on screen and unverifiable in this transcript; Whisper tiny transcript with some mis-heard names (Endel, Indie/Lipa). Survivorship bias is partly acknowledged.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Steve runs App Masters (an agency/podcast) and sells services; sponsor reads (Gusto, Indeed, Quo, Shopify) are ignored.
